questions.question:
The value of tension in a long, thin metal wire has been changed from \({T}_1\) to \({T}_2.\) The lengths of the metal wire at two different values of tension \({T}_1\) and \({T}_2\) are \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) respectively. The actual length of the metal wire is:
1. \(\dfrac{T_1 l_2-T_2 l_1}{T_1-T_2}\)

2. \(\sqrt{T_1 T_2 l_1 l_2}\)

3. \(\dfrac{l_1+l_2}{2}\)

4. \(\dfrac{T_1 l_1-T_2 l_2}{T_1-T_2}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(Y=\left(\dfrac{F}{A}\right)\dfrac{l}{\Delta l} \) Step: Find Young’s modulus for both cases. For tension \(T_1\),\(Y = \dfrac{T_1/A}{(l_1-l)/l} = \dfrac{T_1l}{A(l_1-l)}\) For tension \(T_2\),\(Y = \dfrac{T_2l}{A(l_2-l)}\) On equating both expressions: \(\dfrac{T_1}{l_1-l} = \dfrac{T_2}{l_2-l} \\ \Rightarrow T_1(l_2-l) = T_2(l_1-l) \\ \Rightarrow T_1l_2 - T_2l_1 = (T_1-T_2)l \\ \Rightarrow l = \dfrac{T_1l_2-T_2l_1}{T_1-T_2}\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

Hint:\(T \propto \Delta l\) Step:Find the original length of the wire. Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.
